Description
Customer ID
Customer ID (CID)
Ipv
IPV4 or IPV6
CommandLine
The command line used to create this process
ConnectionDirection
1-inbound2-outbound
EventType
The specific kind of firewall event. Potential
values:FirewallRuleIP4MatchedFirewallRuleIP6MatchedFirewallRuleApplicationFailed
Flags
Indicates whether the event will be reported in Endpoint security > Firewall > Activity - the matched rule has Watch mode
enabled.Monitor - The matched rule is in a firewall policy with Monitor mode enabled.
HostName
Host name
ICMPCode
8-bit decimal value for the ICMP Type field. '*' for "Any type". '0' when unused.
ICMPType
8-bit decimal value for the ICMP Code field. '*' for "Any code". '0' when unused.
ImageFileName
The image file name involved
LocalAddress
Local address involved
LocalPort
Local port involved
MatchCount
This field is the same as MatchCoundSinceLastReport, used for older sensor versions. Will be deprecated.
MatchCountSinceLastReport
The number of matches on the rule since the last time it was sent to the cloud. Events are bounded once per hour, so it
should be the number of times the rule was matched in the last hour.
NetworkProfile
Windows network location profile
PID
Process ID of the process that initiated the traffic.
PolicyName
Name of the firewall policy matched
PolicyID
The unique ID of the firewall policy matched
Protocol
An 8-bit decimal value for matching against IP protocol field
RemoteAddress
Remote address involved
RemotePort
Remote Port involved
RuleAction
The action taken on the activity:1: allowed2: blocked0: invalid - for example, the rule specifies traffic on a non-existent disk
drive
RuleDescription
Description of the rule
RuleFamilyID
Identifier that corresponds to a rule’s Version in the console. Changes each time a rule is edited.
RuleGroupName
Name of the rule group the matched rule belongs to
RuleName
Name of the rule
RuleID
Identifier assigned to the rule when created. Always stays the same.
